I can't answer this. Whether a political party is "to blame" for high rents is a matter of political judgment, and the StatCan tools only return statistics. They can't assign responsibility to a party or tell you which policies caused rent levels.

The statistics can describe rent trends, and you could draw your own conclusions from them. My search for a rent-specific table was not conclusive: the results were weak matches (a CPI basket-weights table and CPI core-inflation tables), so I can't confirm any of them tracks rent. I'd suggest searching Statistics Canada for the rent component of the Consumer Price Index. For party platforms and housing policy, look to party documents and independent policy analysis.
